column3: The Hebrew leaves the attackers unnamed; BSB identifies them as the Israelites.
The Hebrew explicitly calls them “the people” twice and has no separate noun “meat” or adverb “greedily”.
The Hebrew uses an active plural “they told” and leaves Saul unnamed as the speaker of the reply; BSB has “someone reported” and repeats Saul.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul, joins ox and sheep with “and”, and says each ox was in its owner’s hand; BSB uses “he”, “or”, and omits the hand.
The Hebrew uses the verb for beginning to build; BSB expresses it as the first time he built an altar.
The Hebrew leaves those replying unnamed and asks to draw near to God; BSB identifies troops and explicitly describes consulting God.
The Hebrew leaves the nonanswering subject implicit; BSB repeats God’s name.
The Hebrew calls the leaders corners and directs them to know and see; BSB uses “let us investigate”.
The Hebrew says no one answered him; BSB says no one said a word.
The Hebrew does not repeat Saul’s name initially but names him as the audience of the reply; BSB does the reverse and calls the people troops.

The Hebrew has only a brief request after addressing the LORD, without BSB’s question about no answer and separate conditions for Urim and Thummim. It says the people went out, rather than explicitly naming a charge.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Jonathan as Saul’s audience and has no separate “only” before tasting. Its final statement is “Here I am; I will die”, without an explicit question particle.
The Hebrew says God should do thus and add thus, without an explicit “punish me” or negative “if you do not”.
The Hebrew says he acted “with God” and uses the redeeming verb for what the people did; BSB has “with God’s help” and “rescued”.
The Hebrew names Saul’s upward movement and says the Philistines went to their place; BSB gives giving up pursuit and returning to their land.
The Hebrew uses the names Moab and Edom; BSB gives their peoples.
The Hebrew has singular “hand” and singular “his plunderer”; BSB uses plural “hands” and “plunderers”.
The Hebrew repeats the noun “name” for both daughters; BSB combines their naming.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular “son of Abiel”; BSB has plural “sons of Abiel”.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Saul as the observer and calls a brave man a “son of strength”; BSB uses “he” and “brave man”.
